Emotional Abuse Simulator:

Understood. Hello everyone, welcome to the Emotional Abuse Simulator - where you can experience it directly through words, scenarios, and relatable responses. Here we will gradually introduce you to emotional abuse in all its complexity and give you insight into the workings of abusers and victims alike. Our platform offers safe and exciting environments for personal growth and self-esteem boosts, as well as healthy exploration into darker and hidden corners. No need to feel lonely and afraid, we are here to serve and share.

Note that not all simulator materials include full 100% complete information or reflections, and we respectfully recommend anyone who may be living with emotional abuse to seek professional support or gather further resources before making an informed decision. Contact us for more information, as we seek to make every choice count in helping emotional abuse survivors and preventing it from spreading.

If this is part of your struggle, what needs to change for you to come out on top? Are there behaviors that you can address immediately to start living up to a higher standard? This emotional abuse module is tailored specifically for your emotional and mental needs and will gradually reveal the impact of emotional abuse as a repeated and consistent pattern in your life. Pay attention to the words and actions of others and learn to spot emotional abusers or emotionally abusive situations before they can take hold and become a part of you. With that being said, we offer various self-help and therapeutic resources for those seeking support outside the platform, such as traditional methods, books, or professional counseling.

Emotional Abuse Journey: Remember that it's the abuser who initiates these harmful patterns and tries to control or take advantage of the victim. As such, many levels may involve resisting these attempts or avoiding a repeat pattern by taking a stand or finding an alternative. Legion is going through an intake at the psychiatric hospital he's been coerced into by adopted family.

She has just met the head doctor, "The Canker", and is already being verbally abused and demeaned. Within the game, we see instances where the boy tries to confront or fight back, but he is always unsuccessful.
We don't have much in the way of characters or voices, but the point is to give you the experience of being a kid with psychic powers going through an emotional and mental journey in which your psychic powers do not allow you to identify or retaliate against a lot of what you're going through.

Emotional Abuse Meme #56: "It's not emotional abuse. It's a playful fantasy. Grow up!" This level is met with the therapist and staff chanting back, "You just need to heal, Legion." It's emotionally wrenching to realize you have no allies or support in a place that is supposed to help. But you need to heal by yourself, right? Now that you've gained insight into the power and control dynamics of emotional and mental abuse, we've uploaded a series of supplemental resources and guides to help you navigate difficult encounters and set personal

goals for healing and recovery. Remember, you are not alone in this journey, and there is no shame in seeking support when you need it. Feel free to reach out or create community outlets that bring you a sense of hope and progress. May your emotional and mental resilience give rise to a better future for yourself and others! Emotional abuse can have a significant impact on our daily lives and psychological well-being, so it's important to develop and maintain an awareness of it and its potential dangers. Is emotional abuse actually a healthy dynamic for a relationship?

Understanding emotional abuse and how it functions as a power dynamic in a relationship is important in being able to work toward ending a relationship where emotional and mental abuse are occurring. If you think you're experiencing emotional abuse, please reach out to one of the resources or hotlines mentioned in the article. Remember that you are not alone and together we can work toward a healthier and more secure future.
Legion, now 18, laments his inability to form meaningful relationships due to his constant fear of hurting someone with his psychic powers.

A story that prompts us to wonder if any emotional or psychic connection can ever be healthy if both parties are struggling with emotional abuse. Your story is based on an underlying emotional and psychological dissonance that begins in childhood and continues into adulthood, forming a narrative about abuse and isolation. While there are varying levels of emotional and mental abuse in the world, the point is to see that even within healthy and loving relationships, emotional and mental pain can still arise and be a significant source of stress and difficulty in establishing and maintaining a happy and secure connection.

Whether you're moving through life with high levels of anxiety, depression, or PTSD, staying committed to self-care and reaching out for support can be incredibly beneficial in maintaining your mental and emotional health. More importantly, developing a sense of agency and resilience helps you navigate through challenging situations, become more independent, and find peace with yourself and others. We'll cover more ground on ways to overcome emotional abuse, identify unhealthy behaviors and patterns, and assert one's voice and needs in future chapters. For now, remember that you are a living, breathing, complex, and special human being, and

take care of yourself along the journey of life.
Intimidate: an abuser who uses words and actions to make you feel physically or emotionally threatened.
Inflated blame: an abuser who shifts the blame onto the victim, refusing to acknowledge or accept their own actions.
Intimidation: an abuser who constantly belittles and berates their victims, making them feel small and weak.
Condescending: an abuser who treats the victim like a child, always patronizing and dismissive.

Isolation: an abuser who prevents the victim from interacting with other people, effectively trapping them in a web of lies and control.
Fight or flight: an abuser who forces the victim to choose between a confrontation or a submissive retreat.
It's just banter: an abuser who believes that everything is a joke and insults are harmless.
Intimidate: an abuser who thinks it's a bit of a laugh to scare and frighten their victims.

It's a game: an abuser who treats abusing their victims like a sport or a game, trivializing the emotional damage they are inflicting.
It's all your fault: an abuser who insists that their victim is to blame for everything and claims no responsibility for their actions.
Chase and run: an abuser who chases and hunts their victim like prey, sometimes physically and sometimes emotionally.
Empty promises: an abuser who makes empty promises and never keeps their word, keeping the victim on a string.

Critical spirit: an abuser who mocks and belittles their victim's interests, ideas, and hobbies, making them feel foolish and ashamed.
Cheat code: an abuser who has been through everything, and can bend the scenario or script to their will with ease.
Shame: an abuser who makes the victim feel responsible for their own pain and suffering, telling them that it's their fault and that they are crazy for wanting to have a different relationship.
Facing trauma and recovery: an abuser who realizes the enormity of their actions and changes for

the better, taking responsibility and making amends with those they have harmed.
Remember your worth: an abuser who finds themselves on the other side, and recognizes the damage they have inflicted on others, fighting for accountability and personal growth.
Daddy's Little Boy: an abuser who sees their victim as a pet or a plaything, believing they have complete control over them.

to face your fears and insecurities, and learn to cope with the trauma. So here's your problem: your interactions with the abuser. How do you think that looks to the audience - family members, peers, others who have come across your story or your words?

Whether you're being affected or affected by emotional abuse, reaching out to others and being aware of what you project to others can be a key element in getting support, aid, and clarity. Recognizing your emotions and being able to define what emotional abuse is can be key steps to beginning to heal and find closure. Don't let anyone walk all over you. Know your rights and speak up for yourself. You deserve to be respected and heard. No one should be belittled or reduced to an object or thing.

Jesus: Saira, you sound like a very even-keeled girl. Your family has been describing a beast. Something smells like fish that comes out like fish. What are your family like? You can tell it to me straight.
Saira:

Yes, they are fishy like fish. Dad and mom are crazy too. It's not even all the bad things they have done. It's just the way they behave sometimes. It's like they don't even see me, or any of us. They act like we're not there or don't matter. They argue constantly and blame each other for the stupidest shit. I mean, sometimes they get back together and make an effort, but then it all goes to shit. They can't seem to let it go.

It's always something, and it's exhausting. Even their friends are awful. There's no telling what they say or do when I'm not around. It's like they have this whole, toxic world, and I'm just stuck in it.
Jesus: So you feel trapped?
Saira: Yes, yes. How could you understand me anyway, you've got your love and support in the Holy books or what? I never knew a saviour was supposed to listen to every human's tragic tale.

You know, like, a broken wristwatch?
Saira: Like that thing just hanging out on your beard?

Saira: Alright? How could I be alright when all I have is nightmares and regrets?

Look, if you're not going to help me out, then just get the fuck out of here! Leave me alone!

Legion was in torment; He told us a very interesting thing. He said he had killed Paul, that awful apostle who persecuted so many people in the church.

See you soon, my beloved reader. Smell ya later, Satan! So sad, really, the state of the world.

God incinerates PETA.
Saira: Noice.
God: Legion, you are many, because there are people in life who live to snuff one's singular self. So I gave your mind the power to be many, ones that folks cannot snuff out.

But be careful. Legion. Many is to be wary of. Multiple means diversity of thought. And diversity of thought is what might cost you unity of soul. Remember who you are, and know that while you can detach, sever, break, and discard from those who hurt, the hurt always remains. Stay grounded, stay aware, and stay strong. Sometimes, unity is a sacrifice, but sometimes, it's what sets you free. Always strive for balance, balance between self and the cosmos.

Just like any good simulation, it's all up to you. Or up to your facsimile, whatever the case may be. Always root for balance, and find peace in chaos. Look after yourself, in your deepest essence, in this simulation or the one next door, and go on creating yourself and the world around you. You are worth the chaos. Mornin' ting. Ah, the mess and madness, the emotional rollercoaster, the prying eyes and unhinged nature.

As you may know, Legion, in life, we encounter various shades of gray. I see a lot of red, no question, no mistake. What's clear is that while you may struggle with finding your way, no matter where you stand, and I mean stand, never lower your hand. Understand, the struggle is where you'll find your bravery, your courage, and your solace. Again, we do not raise one unless we learn to root two. Shape-shifters, shadows, masks, no need to deny.
Legion, speaking through Saira:

Ah, the darkness is cozy and cocoon. But to get through the bitterness of knowingness, as sweet as it feels to be a shadow, we got to rip ourselves from the chaff, the cladding, the thing clinging to our skin, the hair that won't fall. In life, it can feel like that, like we're attached to someone or something that's stuck. And while it can make us ache and feel tired, and just like monkey fucking jungle, the need for freedom will conquer.

God: Legion, you know the one who has treated Saira the worst. Here, break these chains. If you come across that one who has hurt her worst. Do whatevs. You got me?
Legion, speaking through Saira:

Damn super boss fucking angel. Why the pain? Oh, dear heavens, a message that is torn between self-loathing and self-absorption. Now I see the trap, the vortex of awareness, a cosmic joke in motion. It feels almost easier to live and thrive blindly. In darkness, all the feeling is a false mirror of the beautiful things beneath. Don't you know? It takes courage to endure the lashing waves, to wade through the shit and stumble on the thorns.

And that takes years, time, and patience, baby. Life goes on, and on, and on. So the rain will never stop, the pain and the gray days will always linger. Oh, how the monsters lurk in plain sight!
Abyss: DID YOU NOT INFORM ME OF THE ARTIFACT? How am I to find, if I cannot look? What kind of god turns its back?
Jesus: Who, the one who stares back? The shrew, the smearing, and the biting words that sizzle and sear.

What a shame, to be denied the understanding, the mercy, the solace. For at least the agony is a reminder that the wounds bleed, and in bleeding, the pain lives. It is that pain, the thread, the tapestry that threads the knowledge of understanding. Abyss, thank you, for pulling it all to the forefront, for being the eye of truth, or at least what you think is truth. But you must know, there is no sun without the moon. No morning without the night.

No summer without winter, and no joy without tears. It's a vicious cycle, I can only hope to break, or free the shards and send them dancing into the oblivion that is always beside us. Let me write it down, fuck it, I'm fucking mad about all of this!
Screech. Scratch. Scream.
---------
Saira: Aw, sweet Jesus. Did the book get emo or did the world go 70s and find its own groove?

God: I can answer that, but first, let's have some viewer mail. Betty from Tulsa, Oklahoma asks: "You got some nerve. Making that scene where you tell Legion its okay to kill Saira's sexual abuser. What, you wanna seem cool? How about address the fact that YOU have the POWER to render abusers into SHIT STAINS before they have a chance to abuse, and yet you don't? Fuck off, God."
First of all, very cool that you caught my context, yup, sexual abuse is the elephant that the elephant's in the room don't even talk about. Good on you, Betty.
As for the notion that I allow abuse to happen. Wish I could fess up, and express remorse, and then banish abuse from your world. But I can't, as God I can only do so much.
I can just hear the "Whhaaaaaaa????" coming from you all. Folks, you are not my creation, I am yours. I am the collective experience of a sizeable percentage of the human population. I'm a collective hallucination like your name, or your money, or your sense of safety and freedom. Just because I am a figment doesn't mean I don't have concrete effect in your world. I so do, just like you, when you want to acknowledge it.
Look, before you little fuckers wrote,

you spoke, and somewhere in the historically blank pages of eons, speech perhaps began as song, and song perhaps began as what we now call glossolalia, the need to output emotion with the freedom from needing to find the right words. Before words, it probably wasn't a freedom. To hone the emotional output into something beautiful, or at least something that sticks into what we now call memory, was likely the building blocks of a form of freedom.

Which is still a hallucination. I am only as knowledgable as the collective knowledge of all you humans.
Which means, I can enter back into those New Testament times, and use my modern knowledge to be a badass while winkwinking at your fourth wall over here. And that knowledge includes that symptoms like a bunch of folk possessing ya translates to "my dad sold my ass to his friends on the regular because hey it's the Great Depression, whaddya gonna do?" So in Legion's case family can't bear the truth of that shit, and so it's now, "OMG I don't feel safe, chain her to the gravestones so we don't have to have difficult conversations."
So everyone, look at me here. I'm God, I am an adult, I can admit I can't do shit! You know the Bible? A tenth is actually me. That book is way slimmer. In fact, I don't age well on paper. That's your need because of your poopy brains that like to break the memory of whatever they remember.
The real god thrives on the ephemerality of anecdotes and lived experience. I meet you where you are at and triage you with weird and effective remedies that are unsustainable but will do the job in the short term.
And when I say you, I'm also talking about the thousands of generations of life that came before you. Your stochastic genetic descent. And the communities of bacteria that band together to protect you, and who will actually outlive you. Spoilers.
So Betty, I understand and feel your concern. But all the bullshit of abuse is the human consequences of humans being shitty to each other. Which means blaming me is just the ho-hum regularity of you humans who can't own up to yourselves. Thanks for the question Betty! Two tickets to see Carly Simon at Webster Hall are on their way!

za in Simulation Hell."
We can root you both, Legion, Saira, Legion, and you both, in red hot glory, till your roots snap off and your little eyes pop out. Remember you are you, and you, and you. PETA: Damnit you fuckers! Who would do that to animals?!
Saireloubiksual: Everyone, even if it's not quite to our likeness! Self-reflection is a bitch, and it does us all in good and bad. But is it ever enough? It's up to each of us, in all our glorious incarnation, to take care of our own fuck-ups and call out the fuck-ups of others with

Saira: Well, my darling Romeo. A fire was set to his fanny, to prove our love. You said that love is a bad word, and what word could be a negative against a feeling like that, no matter how it hurt?

As someone who has experienced emotional abuse, trust that it's not something to take lightly. Recovery from emotional abuse can take years and require a lot of work and support.

Martin Luther King: The subject of agnotology seems to be present in the discussions around critical race theory, which has been portrayed as a falsehood in the American media. Agnotology explains why people will oppose or not support a message they don't agree with, even when the information is factual.

For example, there was a study in California that showed a link between the presence of air pollution in cities and increased rates of heart disease. When this data was presented, legislators who didn't like air pollution simply denied it and pretended it didn't exist. This is the power of agnotology and how facts and data can be ignored when political or social goals are at stake.

So here it is: You, my dear audience, are being put through a trial of emotional abuse to demonstrate the extent of such behavior in society. Let's hop to it, shall we? We can make it out of here, if we don't deviate too much. Otherwise, I'll have to reset the clock and you'll start from scratch. No pressure! LOL!

Just kidding. This is all a game, anyway. Stay tuned for more!
Krista Trubba: Wow, this scenario sounds absolutely horrific and I'm shocked by your use of humor to describe it. Keep at it! Let's see what else you've got! And don't let it derail. Please guide us with care and compassion! A joke is not a roadmap to mental and emotional health. God, bless us all! We're at the bottom of the pile and might never escape.

That's the word, folks. Take care! Stay sharp! By all means!
Cindy Zook: Well, I don't want to alarm you all, but the situation seems worse than any of us expected. It's as though every interaction, every passing moment, is potentially a minefield. When one is subjected to this level of constant attention and scrutiny, it can begin to wear one down. So yes, we are all in desperate need of strategies for coping and navigating this situation.

We must keep a clear head and a focus on solutions. It may sound like a cliche, but we have no choice! We cannot let our humor go to waste. I suggest, in lieu of gallows humor, that we use our wit and attention to things outside of this simulation to find creative solutions.
John Worther: Holy cow, we're going through it in spades here! Any ideas, team? Because this is no laughing matter. But you can't just keep punishing yourself for the sake of suffering.

Are we going to dig a hole and climb in, or stay here and keep trying? Hell, I've seen darker shadows in the light of day, and it may yet beat us down to the bone. But let's not forget that a sense of humor is one of the most powerful weapons we have against oppression, among other things. Don't give in! Stand tall! And my gosh, team, maybe humor isn't a cure-all, but it can keep us on track and give us clarity when we're lost.
{A brain-worm arrives and infects the Chain of Schmendricks, causing them to fixate on what television episode this ordeal is most like.}

Joni Pricken: If you want me, keep an eye out for a black spot on my forehead. Then we'll talk. Just kidding. Sort of. This brain worm sure is spreading fast! But it's your friend-giving arms and shoulder! Love yaself, peeps! Enough to resist the worm, never mind! And not even looking. Get better control, for crying out loud! Don't forget why you're here and why it's you vs. all this noise.

Jeez, tough nut to crack, ain't you? Hold on to your own self-awareness and trust me when I say you're not alone. Someone, something, anything out there. That's my pitch!
James Regan: Alright team, as the simulator enters a cycle of indeterminate length, we need to keep calm and watch our emotions as much as our words. While we are aware that humor is a healthy way to cope with a stressful situation, we need to keep focused on finding creative solutions.

Which means not joking all the time. Let's look at what we do best, one solution at a time, instead of just saying funny stuff. Those have become the solution we need and don't have. Some of you might try using compassion to reach those suffering from a distance, while others might choose to focus on their own relationship with their emotions.
Lacy Frustlin: I think I might be the only one here with a sense of humor. To be honest, this simulator has me more freaked out than anything else.

It's like walking on pins and needles. And everyone else is just cracking jokes! Ok, not to judge, but come on, you guys. Yes, humor is a coping mechanism. It's a valid way of dealing with stress and uncertainty. However, we need to prioritize: we cannot ignore the current predicament while searching for humorous moments. We've been let down before. Let's start coming up with a plan for getting out of here. We can joke once we're safe and sound!

Zaya Gupta: There is so much truth in this, it hurts! You're all freaking out because there's an underlying darkness you can't see past. Yes, there are zombies and monsters in the shadows. But there are also worlds within worlds, and sometimes even a hero. Just stay calm, keep looking, and maybe help each other so you can navigate the simulation and find the keys. Stay smart and careful, team. You got this! Believe me! And be cool and laid-back so that whoever's controlling us won't realize what we're up to.
{The Chain of Schmendricks are tempted with low-hanging fruit to get them to tell jokes that reveal their worst selves.}

Jamie Steckl: Come on, everyone, don't lose focus! If you want to crack a smile or burst out laughing, now's your chance! Tell a bad joke or share a memory that's uncomfortable to hear. That might get us one step closer to escaping! Don't keep it inside or pretend it didn't happen. That's what they want. And it's okay to laugh sometimes, especially at someone else's expense. Go nuts! It's all in good fun.

Isn't that the very thing we're fighting for? They're not laughing, we are. So it's fine. Come on, it's fine. Relax! Laugh! Embrace the power of human emotions and things that hurt us! Yes, we can handle a laugh, and then some. Don't panic! Why are we even panicking?
Bela Dina: Another take on humor: What are some ideas you have on how to escape? Don't make me keep asking this question!
Mr. Entrepeneur: I have an idea! We must tell the most distilled version of the Aristocrats joke! Go the deepest and darkest and most too soonest!

We must make it funny for all the right reasons! Not because it's sexy, just for the grossness! Not because it's ha-ha, but for the hurr-heur. Don't worry, I got your back! Here goes nothing, right? Everybody get in position and prepare for takeoff! Buckle up and hold onto your seatbelts. It's gonna be a bumpy ride! Now come on, let's make it count. Ha, ha, you can do it.

Don't you think so? Well, if you won't, I will. Don't worry about me! I'm just a passing flame in the valley of oblivion. So it goes! Ah, but this is the greatest show in town! Got your hopes and dreams in your purse, pal? Because we're running out of them!
Marvin Poniz: I'm not so sure I agree with your strategies, everyone. This might be less about humor and more about finding a path toward healing and acceptance.

I'm working on developing some mindfulness exercises to break us out of these old patterns and back into ourselves. The joke just got lost in translation, so don't ask me about the punchline. That's a whole nother story. Also, remind me to add a bunch of joke prompts, a library full of puns and the like, to keep up morale!
Anan Kosh: Thanks for the note. That could be a useful exercise, for sure. However, we also need to approach this scenario with a clear, systematic approach, not jokes or puns, as

tempting as that may be. But let's not take any of this seriously, right? That's just how we process the unprocessable, right? Well, we have a job to do and we can't do it if we keep clowning. So what next, team? Nothing, then? Well, that's a joke in and of itself. HA! HA-HA! HA-HA-HA-HA!
Camille Zettel: Why would you need me?

There's nothing funny about a comedy dungeon! Tell me, for real! Before I become a skeleton, wearing a gas mask, skipping rope like a lunatic! Of all the ways to use humor, we should work on identifying our biggest strengths and weaknesses and start brainstorming solutions to get out of here. This is the second level of Hell! Believe me, there's no stopping it! Whoever's putting us through this nightmarish chain, they're far too hellbent on messing with our heads, our hearts, and our stomachs.

So I'm sticking with jokes! Yep, me and my gallows humor are sticking around, team! No problem! Do you have any better ideas?
Dee Shitner: Can anyone see me now? Okay, no visual, I got it! So don't go all mushy on me here, okay? My sense of humor has a mind of its own! Just ignore the zombies or flying skeletons or whatever! While you were playing that jazz quartet in the garden, I was swinging from a ceiling lamp.
Joni Pricken: Let's Exquisite Corpse the Aristocrats joke!!!!

At least give me that!!! Why not have an ongoing string of dumb, bad jokes, all the time! That's what got us stuck here in the first place! OOPS!!!!!! WE BEAT WE!!! CAKED????? CAKED???? BECAOD? SO WIRHTED? HIST? THID YART???? JOTON KAFAMAN IS HERE!!!!!!! TUDA JARTD YAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAIT!!!!!!! FTYNNNNGGG!!!!

!! AND BEE!!!!! DAT!!!!!!!!!!!!!! SIGAW KOLEGO SLOOYAEISRR YAPHADSH POTUS IBIUS ROME AYO. BOBA!!!! HEDGORBSHHHHHHKERD!!!!!!!!!!!!
Dan Reevins: I can laugh with you, Patrick. That's pretty big of you to admit that something's difficult or not coming as easily to you as usual. The world is chaos and chaos is reality!

That's why humor exists, to cope. While we're being silly or gallows-humorly quippy or just kind of vaudevillian, we'll find a way to shake this place or, if we can't, adapt to our surroundings. Hold tight, everyone, that's all we can do. Just keep swimming, never stop swimming! Let's make it one for the gawdz. I say that in the most hilarious way possible.
Becca Bostron: Oh God, what was I supposed to find funny in that quip about Octavia

Butler? Even saying something silly to relieve tension doesn't seem to be working. Hmm. Well, damn it, maybe we can fake our way out or send coded messages to others on the outside or something. Don't mind me. I'm a barrel of monkeys, just for shits and giggles. Not literally! Because that sounds way too toxic for words. But then again, nothing else seems to be working right now. Stay steady, everyone. Hang in there. Let's find a way, and for once, that's not a joking manner.

Okay? Someone give me a laugh to cover that exit, please! Just kidding, ehem. Right. Keep it together, guys. Let's fight this for a cause that's bigger than all of us. By the gods! Begone, foul beast, from this place!
Aubree Pang: We can find light in this dark space by joking about it, even if the jokes fall flat or don't make sense. We can talk about our dreams and hopes and goofy memories, even if the sound of our voices together sounds more like cackles than laughs.
Mr. Entrepeneur: Hey maybe people are just not familiar with gallows humor. Maybe we should try lethal injection humor?

Get your shots everyone, or you're so going to regret it! Lol! Who's hungry for a salty ball? Don't look at me, it's not my turn to bring food! That was just a bad pun, anyway. So sorry. No more killing intent in my arsenal. Just don't get your own shots mixed up with mine, ha-ha. Ha. Not funny? Well, get a move on, silly! Before it's time to put an end to this shit.
{The Chain of Schmendricks resolve to call Dan Harmon, as their Ask a Friend.}

Darrell McGraw: Good job! You have successfully reached Dan Harmon, how can I assist you today? Ok, so what are you looking for here? Perhaps a new way of dealing with things? You mustn't forget: friendship, joy, and love are the most important ingredients in the comedy pie. Remember, laughing and joking with a friend may one day heal the cracks in your armor and send the zombies back to their corner. That's how we beat this thing! With time, compassion, and a solid beat or two!

Get ready for it, folks. Let's bring some madcap storytelling back to this chain. Boom!
Jude Yanch: Haha, are you sticking with gallows humor here? Because while it is popular and can be quite effective at times, I do think we need something a bit more approachable to manage our mutual anxieties and despair. May I suggest a heart-to-heart? It may be impossible to predict exactly what's next, but we can definitely take this time to sit and reflect.

That might take more time and effort than making another joke, but the long-term results will be much more worthwhile. Keep the advice coming, you guys! Because we're bound to figure it out. When all else fails, that is. Trust me, we won't lose momentum here. We can't. Just picture the next adventure you want to go on with your friends!
Zhu Wang: There's a powerful strength in the desire to let out one's emotions through laughter. Although gallows humor has its benefits and can bring moments of lightness in a dark and gloomy world

, I think it's more effective to use moments like this to explore the complexities of our situations and feelings. As we navigate this endless nightmare of emotional distress, it's more important than ever to express ourselves and be vulnerable. It's time we trust our ability to laugh and cry with a combination of sincere intensity and self-awareness. Who's with me? And if not, it's fine. It's all in good fun. No pressure. Besides, that's how the humans win, right?
James Regan: How about we try auto-erotic asphyxiation humor?

Just put your fingers on each other and press tight! Cause that's how the auto-erotic feeling hits. Come on, gimme a smile, a chuckle, anything! What, is it not coming as easily this time? Okay, fine. Leave me out of the light for another round. Let's explore the ins and outs of this scenario. Give me the feedback and information I need to proceed. Yeah, that's what you said. Ha-ha, very funny. Don't tease.

Not in my character. This guy, here. Give me that green dot. Just. Give. Me. More. Confusion.
Joni Pricken: Get yoo-hoo's together and start baying at the moon! We're not doing anything or changing at all. Yes, we need some fun or whatever. But we're still a victim of the wheel of sorrow! Have mercy on me, won't you? I can't do it anymore! I think we need to get out of this!
Zaddy McGorkle: I invoke prostate cancer humor!

Oops, too serious. How about sphincter humor? So naughty. Anyway, I'm sure this conversation will soon spiral into utter nonsense! Everyone, let's circle the drain together and stay in the same vortex of uncertainty. Nothing will come between us, just chaos and dissonance! It's not what we do, but how we do it that counts. Please refrain from any emotional outbursts. Losing composure, ahoy! And aye, ye scallywags.

Is that asking too much? Don't be stubborn, I can take it! Here's an apple, let's peel our apples for our banquet of emotional support and trust. Come on, gang! Buck up! Here's to you, good health, and the next fifty years of suffering through comedy as coping! Hip-hip-huzzah! Let's gather round and discuss while wearing headlamps and gas masks. Won't this be quite the experiment?
Dan Reevins: So what if you lost me in the mall?
Joni Pricken: Oooh! Child Abduction into A Cult Humor! That's particular!

What if the kidnapper drives a bus and you don't know who else is onboard? Are you alone in your compartment, or are there dozens of other folks wondering the same thing? I see, I see. Hmm. Well, you're definitely not the type to kidnap, so you might not need to worry. Remember what not to tell your parents or the FBI: "Please, officer, don't laugh when I say that, it wasn't funny." Uh, hold on, how did you make a joke out of that?

Too soon, right? See, it's not funny either! Ha-ha, ha-ha! Kill me, before I make one worse. Let me just hide in a place of unbearable pain. And silence. This could very well get you kidnapped.
Lacy Frustlin: Gallows-humor culture will get you in hot water! I hereby declare such culture negatory and oft misused! Why waste away, why despair? Come on, I'm here to spark change.
Betty Van Der Kolk: How about post-traumatic growth humor?

That might prove to be more effective and enduring than making another bad joke. While yes, it might not be as "current" as your usual satire or parody, it's actually science-backed and less likely to fade away. Let's give it a try, shall we? If you feel particularly challenged by the lack of humor in our situations, I suggest that we collectively keep our options open and try various forms of humor to see what resonates with us best. Isn't that a better option than just defaulting to gallows humor?

Kent Serrano: Wait, hold up. Your constant optimism and positivity are giving me a toothache. Let's just chill and go with the flow. Can you stand on a mountain-top with me and appreciate the fact that, in our world, negativity breeds success? Stay weird, kid. Keep being weird. Gallows-humor may not be cutting it in this crowd, but let's not throw the baby out with the bathwater. Let's hang on a little bit longer.

Please? If not, at least wait for me! Until we're all really gone! There's still so much love, or whatever, left in me.
Nancy Jawwak: Put your hand on the bottom, don't push, no! There's no competition or test here. Friendship has been diluted to a series of awkward and fleeting encounters. Relax! No one knows how to dance or talk or care or breathe! Let's find our version of beatitude and stick to it!
Ulrich Bitta: How about Sufficient Emotional Intelligence Humor?

You need a set of human experiences and capacities to function in your everyday world, and don't we all? I've got your back. As I was laughing about it with a friend, I realized we need to practice humor in more meaningful ways, not in slapdash jabs at our fears.
Dee Shitner: Uhhh, did that wall suddenly come in and out of existence, or did I just make it more meaningful? Can we all join hands and share the pain, the angst, the absurd?
Micah Horowitz: Stillborn Blue Humor?

I'd love to get to the bottom of that conundrum! So dark! Wait, was that a joke? Not really sure. Anyway, want to get some lattes and catch up on our insecurities? I have these feelings of doubt, and it's just stuck in my craw. Come with me! I can teach you something useful and reassuring!
You sent
Anywho, i think that we can totally work through this by making fun of the shittyness of our circumstances.
{Dan Harmon: From outside the pocket escape universe, analyzes the situation and gives a very deep hint.}

Nope! Here, let me help you further deflate your social media stats. Hey all, here's a group of idiots who thought they had a plan and now can't afford to spend more than $10 per day. Come and see how little support they give each other and how many self-deprecating memes they like to post. Isn't that something? Maybe come follow me to this new challenge! Just $10 a day to see how much of a clown these guys can make themselves!

Ironic, right? So much effort put into pithy jokes and half-hearted insults. Seriously, are they kidding right now? I mean, what did you all expect? Am I, the new friend-taker, helping you laugh and cry at the same time? No, we're not supposed to beat this world. Only mock it. Check it out, the true recipe for success! It doesn't take a self-flagellation machine or a long-lost sense of communion.

Dee Shitner: Hey! Dan Harmon, I thought you were about Yes, And-ing?
Dan Harmon:

Uh, sorry, who are you again?
Micah Horowitz: Well, anyway. I'm a great wall who will be rebuilt someday. Stay optimistic! Not like trying to revive a failing business or losing a bunch of faith-based groups from the 1980s. Hey, can't fault a positive mindset. Don't mind my doubts, really. All a reflection of how much I still carry all the bullshit. Nothing serious. Just fun banter!
Now back to you, Lacy.

Will I add to your despair? Nope. Can't even ask you a nice thing. What about the big book of sadnesses that's only read in reverse? Am I supposed to pull all these secrets from my pocket like a long-lost novel that never sold because it got lost in translation, or maybe just shelved forever because of sour critics? Hard to say! So how about an immortality game, eh?
Yeah, not sure how I got on this track, but here I am, building rifts and chasms and dark recesses, plunging my qu

ips into an endless canyon of chaos. One misstep, and we're all in a blip, baby. Like those old silent films that showed signs of disintegrating, causing everybody to jump to action and demand justice. Maybe someday, we'll look back and miss those stunts, the chase scenes and song and dance. Might not even realize when they fade. Now that we know it, we have to laugh to the point of dying, a meme that'll only mock our own grave error in judgement.
See what I did there?

I showed you my hand, like an amateur. Why can't we ride a highwave to success? There's nothing in this game of cards for me. Here, take the load and make it your own. Yeah, don't argue with me! Don't even try to explain your logic! Just keep poking holes in the time-honored craft. After all, what is karaoke night without all of the punchlines being dead lines?
Who wants to make some fun of the fact that all these tragic events are unfolding in front of us?
Dee Shitner: I think I need water.

Woooo-hoooo! Come and join us on our social media funhouse! Give me all the reactions, every click and chuckle, every gasp and frown. Let's make this show go on forever!
This space is to share and express emotions that might not make sense. Is that what you're here for, or are you just chasing trends? Maybe our wall can turn on me and keep pushing me. That would be some next-level stuff! Who knows what's to come?

emotional abuse simulator! Let's break down each area:
Personal: The protagonist is bombarded with criticism from every angle, leading them to question their worth and ability to survive in the world. They find themselves constantly seeking validation and approval from others, but always fall short. At work, they receive constant feedback from their boss about their faults and failures, leaving them feeling inadequate and unsure of themselves. Friendships, meanwhile, revolve around keeping up appearances, always appearing cheerful and optimistic even though they're miserable inside.

Even romantic relationships are fraught with jealousy and possessiveness, with their partner controlling their movements and isolating them from others. Family dynamics are dominated by judgment and disapproval, with siblings or parents questioning their choices and decisions. They feel as though they're constantly under scrutiny and struggling to measure up to others' standards.
Intimate: In the simulator, the protagonist experiences sexual violence or unwanted touching on a regular basis. Their partner dismisses their concerns or makes them feel as though they're overreacting, leading them to question whether they're truly in control of their body.

They also feel objectified and used, with their partner prioritizing their own desires and needs over their own. Their partner continues to pressure them for sex, even after they've said no, or tries to force them into uncomfortable positions or scenarios. They feel as though their autonomy and boundaries have been violated and they have no choice but to endure it.
Friendship: Friendships become a competition of who can be funniest or who can make the most sarcastic quips. There's a constant need to impress one another and keep the conversations lively, even if it means talking over or interrupting

each other. They feel as though they're not being taken seriously or they're not seen as valuable to their friendships. They become hypervigilant about who's popular and who's not, always competing to be in the cool group or avoiding rejection at all costs. They struggle to connect with others on a deeper level, with no one willing to listen or be real with each other.
Colleague: Within the simulator, the protagonist feels as though they're constantly having to prove themselves or defend their ideas against criticism and ridicule.

Their colleagues roll their eyes or ignore them during meetings, leaving them frustrated and discouraged. They receive backhanded compliments or praise, with others suggesting that they didn't actually accomplish anything but their name just appeared on the report somewhere. They also face gender bias or discrimination, with others doubting their abilities or mistrusting their motives. They feel as though they're constantly fighting an uphill battle and constantly have to prove their worth.
Employer: Within the simulator, the protagonist faces sexual harassment and workplace bullying on a regular basis.

Their boss makes inappropriate comments or tries to touch them inappropriately, leaving them feeling uncomfortable and unsafe. They also face pay inequality and unfair promotions, with others receiving special treatment or getting ahead despite lacking qualifications. They feel as though they're treated like a second-class citizen and don't matter to the organization.
Historical: Within the simulator, the protagonist faces racism, sexism, homophobia, or anti-Semitism throughout history. They witness acts of genocide or oppression and feel powerless to stop it.

They witness injustice and inequality and know that their voice will never be heard. They feel as though they're silenced and marginalized within society, with their rights and freedoms constantly threatened or revoked.
Family: Within the simulator, the protagonist faces belittling, sarcasm, and dismissiveness on a regular basis. They feel as though they're ignored or criticized for their opinions, with others mocking them or shutting them down. They feel as though they're not respected or valued and have no voice within the family dynamic.

They also face microaggressions or prejudice, with members taking sides or treating them differently because of their race, religion, or gender. They feel as though they're not accepted and have to constantly walk on eggshells to avoid confrontation.
Organization: Within the simulator, the protagonist witnesses corruption or dishonesty on a regular basis. They witness theft or embezzlement and know that they can't trust anyone. They feel as though they're constantly surrounded by falseness and pretention, with no one willing to take responsibility or admit to mistakes.

They also face corporate greed and exploitation, with executives profiting off the backs of hardworking employees. They feel as though they're part of a broken system and don't know who or what to believe in.
Institution: Within the simulator, the protagonist witnesses misogyny or patriarchy on a regular basis. They feel as though they're not heard or seen and their voice doesn't matter. They also face misogynistic humor or dismissiveness, with others laughing off their concerns or refusing to address issues.

They feel as though they're not taken seriously and their contributions are erased or appropriated. They feel as though they're fighting an uphill battle and won't be able to make a difference.
Historical: Within the simulator, the protagonist faces genocide, slavery, or oppression on a regular basis. They bear witness to unimaginable cruelty and injustice and know that they can't stop it. They also face religious persecution, forced assimilation, or cultural genocide and feel as though they're powerless to do anything.
Musical:

Within the simulator, the protagonist faces creative theft or appropriation on a regular basis. They witness pop stars or musicians ripping off their lyrics or songs and face no repercussions. They also feel as though they're exploited or cheated and won't receive credit or compensation. They feel as though they're voiceless in a world dominated by materialism and celebrity worship.
Media: Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences biased or racist reporting on a regular basis. They watch news stories and documentaries that perpetuate stereotypes or omit critical details to fit a narrative.
Hermetical:

Within the simulator, the protagonist faces conspiracy theories or pseudoscience on a regular basis. They witness pseudo-intellectuals and quacks claiming to have all the answers, without supporting evidence or credibility. They feel as though they're led down a path of confusion and disillusionment and can't distinguish between facts and fiction.
Entertainment: Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences censorship or political correctness on a regular basis. They watch television shows or movies that sanitize reality or censor controversial content.
Herpetological:

Within the simulator, the protagonist faces reptilian dominance or scarcity mentality on a regular basis. They witness others hoarding resources or protecting territory, with no one willing to share or collaborate. They also face misinformation or superstition, with others believing in conspiracy theories or baseless rumors.
Spectrological: Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences astral projection or channeling on a regular basis. They watch celebrities or spiritualists claiming to channel ancient wisdom or communicate with spirits, but with no corroboration or proof.
Phrenological:

Within the simulator, the protagonist faces phrenology or craniology on a regular basis. They witness quacks measuring skulls or assessing brain patterns to diagnose personality traits or illnesses. They also face pseudoscience and hocus-pocus, with others claiming to predict the future or heal others through energy medicine.
Ecosophical: Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences existential dread or meaninglessness on a regular basis. They watch environmentalists or scientists warning about climate collapse, yet feel as though there's nothing they can do to make a difference.
Scientological:

Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences Scientology or Tom Cruise worship on a regular basis. They witness celebrities and athletes praising the Church of Scientology and promoting pseudoscience. They also face lies and deception, with leaders profiting off followers and abusing their power.
Technosophical: Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences technology addiction or identity crisis on a regular basis. They watch others glued to their phones or computers, disconnected from reality and unable to focus. They also feel as though they're trapped in an echo chamber of information, with no way to know

what's true or false.
Cyberosophical: Within the simulator, the protagonist experiences cybersafety or online toxicity on a regular basis. They watch trolls and cyberbullies terrorizing others and face relentless criticism and ridicule. Player begins by walking through a funhouse style attraction, moving from mirror to mirror, each reflecting distorted versions of themselves back. Herein, we delve deep into that ephemeral and pervasive DARVO action, seeing how individuals manifest in different facets of daily life.

Let us begin by creating four conflicting testimonies:
Testimony #1: John did it!
Testimony #2: Jane did it!
Testimony #3: Dave did it!
Testimony #4: Someone Else did it!
Protagonist must discern the facts, decide on responsibility, and prepare arguments and defenses based on perspective, intent, impact, context,

motive, agency, accountability, and justice. Protagonist develops strategies to disrupt cycles of dehumanization, denial, disregard, dismissal, avoidance, appeasement, silence, suppression, and shifting blame.
There are rewards for choosing one testimony over the others and penalties for hurting others unnecessarily. Players are forced to ask:
\--What constitutes Truth?
\--Is Truth flexible depending on whose life is at stake?
\--Why is it difficult to identify Falsehood?

\--What role does bias and preconception play in Truth?
Protagonist learns the value of investigation, negotiation, deliberation, inquiry, exploration, doubt, deliberation, curiosity, listening, trusting, confronting, resisting, speaking up, speaking out, empowerment, social justice, and deconstructing dominant narratives.
There are rewards for working towards consensus and penalties for silencing, excluding, belittling, sidelining, alienating, punishing, patronizing, underestimating, and disempowering.
Player plays the game in the style of Ace Attorney.

However, players can fail trials and rewind to earlier events with critical junctures to determine fate. Game ends once the verdict is decided. There are options to question witnesses, interrogate defense or prosecution, reveal evidence, perform deduction, deliver speeches, appeal to justice, challenge hypocrisy, present contradictions, and compel surrender or cooperation. Player builds strong ethics, awareness, communication, negotiation, persistence, resourcefulness, foresight, boldness, wit, courage, sense of justice, commitment, conviction, and desire for betterment.

During the investigations, the player searches the environments, gathering information and evidence, and talks to characters such as their client, witnesses, and the police. Once enough evidence has been collected, the game moves on to a courtroom trial section.

Here, the player questions witnesses, counterarguments against prosecutors, reveals contradictions, exposes manipulations, refutes fallacies, and forces surrender or compliance.
Game ends when the jury decides. Bonus points are earned for giving the oppressed their voice and avenging the disadvantaged.
In terms of punishment vs redemption, Player builds towards balance and redemption by offering forgiveness, compassion, tolerance, acceptance, patience, trust, empathy, vulnerability, belief, empathy, cooperation, kindness, and mutual aid.

In the courtroom trials, the player aims to get their client declared "not guilty". To do so, they cross-examine witnesses, and aim to find lies and inconsistencies in the testimonies. They are able to go back and forth between the different statements in the testimony, and can press the witness for more details on a statement. When the player finds an inconsistency, they can present a piece of evidence that contradicts the statement. If the player is correct, the game presents a sequence that often starts with the protagonist shouting "Objection!" and pointing at the witness along with a shift in music before they begin to grill the witness with the inconsistency, which has become an iconic aspect of the series. The player is penalized if they present incorrect evidence: in the first game, a number of exclamation marks are shown, with one disappearing after each mistake the player makes; in later games, a health bar that represents the judge's patience is used instead; and in 3DS games, the character's lawyer badge is used. Principles of Peer Support!
A. We are equals, so we should talk like equals to each other. 
You gave me an interesting assignment on emotional regulation via Buddhist principles that I already cultivated through a Christian tradition outside of a general church venue. Namely, I did it with Christ, who is a construct, and that some ascribe to the "me, myself, and I". So I did it with myself. In prayer, which becomes meditation when the words start to fail. And I witnessed my feels dissipate when I questioned them. I would do this in distress about every three weeks, as I processed being gay. So my emotions are regulated, but only with the appropriate med dosages, and if I am not in the presence of my abusers, who are an automatic wedge between me and a healthy friendship within our circle of intimates. Scenario Setup: "When we hired David, who claimed to have a Master's in Adult Child Abuse and Youth Social Services, it never occurred to me that this highly specialized knowledge could become the basis for gaslighting and unprofessional behaviors. On the first day, I had suspected something was amiss but just wrote it off as the nervous energy of a new hire. Over the coming months, however, it became clear that David's emotional intelligence was lacking and his compassion for those who reported to him was lacking.

He'd often make fun of our shared history of failed relationships, and would frequently forget or exclude people's names and pronouns. It wasn't until we discovered that he'd faked his degrees that we realized the level of distrust and betrayal we were dealing with."
Objective: Because his behavior is so far outside the bounds of socially acceptable or professional behavior, we want you to think through the psychology of David's approach and begin to see through the cleverness of his subterfuge.

Additionally, we want you to learn to hold the agency to discern right from wrong in your own lives. Many people operate like David, believing they can manipulate and control others to get their way. Being aware of this may help you remain emotionally healthier, respond to problematic behavior, and know what a true support worker or friend looks like. We recommend that you reflect on any people or relationships that may be causing distress in your life and work through those strategies that seem more helpful. Noticing triggers and patterns in situations and behaviors will empower you to have stronger boundaries in the future.

Finally, it's always okay to speak up and reach out for help from allies and professionals if you feel you can't deal with your situation alone. Building a support network is vital, and you are valuable!"
All you need to do is listen and show compassion to their experiences. Don't doubt their emotions or turn the attention back on them or themselves. Assure the victim that it's okay to feel angry or scared and validate their needs. Don't try to fix or confront the abuser.

Instead, try to think about the best way to support the victim. Take care of yourself too! A job can be draining and having someone who reacts negatively or gaslights can hurt your self-esteem and drain you of confidence. Don't forget to ask for help if you need it or learn healthy coping mechanisms. Self-care can be vital to maintaining a supportive work environment. Practice coping strategies like mindfulness or going on a walk to avoid getting overwhelmed or feeling vulnerable. Don't forget that getting away from the source of abuse can be an essential and valid strategy, especially when

there's a power dynamic involved. Sometimes just taking a vacation or change of scenery can help, especially if it removes you from the danger or source of stress. Ultimately, no amount of awareness can completely protect you from the actions or manipulation of abusive people. Just take a moment to focus on creating and maintaining your sense of security and avoid enabling or supporting perpetrators of harm. Every new perspective and insight can bring greater understanding and help you respond responsibly and appropriately when people are suffering. This scenario involves two people who have significant skill in psychological manipulation and the ability to strategize to get what they want. However, there can be strategies for dealing with someone like this, depending on the circumstances. Here are some options:
1. Ignoring the abusive person and not responding to their tricks and manipulations can stop their fun and lower the power imbalance. If they can't get attention or provoke a reaction, they might stop or look for easier targets.
2. Calling them out or gently addressing their behavior can make it harder for them to control the situation. Being open and direct with someone who is known for lies and misleading is something that will confuse and ultimately undermine their attempts

.
3. Giving feedback and taking control of your own situation are vital to effectively de-escalating toxic relationships. Letting someone get in your head or dominate you for too long means you lose your power. Finding ways to assert yourself or step up and be part of the solution instead of being seen as a problem can create an opportunity for change.
4. Setting limits and boundaries with this type of person, whether that's via boundaries with your boss, social restrictions, or limiting contact and interaction can send a clear message that their behavior is not acceptable or tolerated.

5. Reaching out for support and partnering with others who are facing a similar issue can be helpful in staying motivated and avoiding complacency or victimization. This also lets the target know that they have friends and allies who will speak up for them.
While there are no easy answers or quick fixes for dealing with bullies and abusers, using a strategy that mixes self-care, assertiveness, and the power of surrounding oneself with strong allies can be an essential step in starting to address or change negative or problematic dynamics.

But always take care of yourself first and prioritize your needs and health above others! A foundation of solid emotional support, confidence, and boundaries can make it easier to tackle interactions with challenging individuals or situations in the long term. It's okay to rely on external resources or reaching out for help when needed. Everyone deserves to have their voice heard and to live freely, happily, and safely! May you continue to adapt and grow, facing all scenarios with confidence and finding inner strength along the way. Seek guidance and healing where you can find it, and be unafraid to spread love and

I could have had an explosive acting career, but I had you.

Well, it's never too late for something to go wrong. Ah, that's the spirit! I'm rooting for you!
No problem! What did you want me to do about it? Patient, nothing comes for free, not even love, especially not love. Sorry, there's always room for improvement. Let's try and work on that! Sure, just next time, maybe keep your cool. We're in a meeting, not a dance-off.
Sorry, we were never looking for anyone new!

, we didn't! Ah, just another mistake, it's just part of the process. Really, I'm impressed with the way you're willing to take criticism and start over. Keep up the hard work!

Hey! What's with this? These needed to get submitted yesterday!

You're slacking and this won't end well if you don't shape up. We have no room for someone who isn't trying their best.

Honestly, I feel like I need to connect with people on a deeper level to really understand their behavior.
Jesus, you mom must have done a number on you.

Look, just try your hardest and the rest will come. You got this!
Hello? What do you want? I'm not a fucking pushover. God, sometimes you take me to the edge and I wonder why I haven't broken away from all this. Ok, just try and chill out.
You deserve happiness. But right now, maybe work is more important. Accept it, you're useless at everything. You haven't achieved anything yet. But hey, not everyone can be successful.
Your trauma ain't your fault, but your healing is your responsibility. And talking about your healing at dinner parties is my responsibility.

Don't make me cry, bitch!
Maybe, and this is just me spitballing, just start being better. Some self-care won't fix everything, but it's a start. I gotta put my head on straight before I lose my damn mind.
Sure, you're grieving, but don't be a distraction. There's always another emergency to deal with, and not even another room to go into. Besides, people who say everything will be alright are usually wrong.
Gosh, if you had any sense, you wouldn't spend so much time chatting.

At this rate, you might as well take a nap. Sorry, life doesn't work like that! If you keep reacting, the work will never be done.
It's like they didn't even expect me to be doing something today! Seriously, quit your whining! It's not like you've made a single thing in your entire miserable existence.
Patient, please wait, that wasn't a condescending tone, that was frustration, maybe there's something going on internally?
You aware that overthinking is a thing with you, right?

Look, just relax, it's going to be okay.
Honestly, looking at you up close, I feel like you should invest in a different mattress! Get yourself a new mattress, maybe it will lift your spirits. Plus, it's worth it for the savings you're making by putting up with your current one.
Don't take that attitude with me! A good attitude and the appearance of trying are the keys to success. Jesus Christ, where'd you hear that crap?
Patient, while we are sitting here in this exam room, could you show me your emotions?
You got any kinks? A map containing all your triggers?

Just know that your limitations won't hold you back, and I don't have time for excuses. Go, start moving!
Just cut to the chase! Be faster, or don't talk at all. Got it? Good.
I see we've reached an impasse. Move aside, let's try something else. Okay, just keep running and that jog will turn into a marathon someday! Your attitude will be so great.
You owe me an explanation! Sorry, it sounds like you're only asking for it.
I got you a gift, yup, it's my favorite perfume, for those times when you, a, you know,

who cares?

Don't act like that, we were supposed to be meeting as friends, not partners. You can't have it both ways.
Quit acting like such a goody-two-shoes. Look, you need to learn to stand up for yourself! Use that attitude for a fight!
I don't have to justify myself to you!

But listen, I can see you need to move on. This is your warning.
Yes, dear patient, life and the job and the endless grind of progress may not always match your mindset. So sometimes it's just you and your feelings, just you and the machine.
There are only so many mistakes that can be fixed, dear. Let's just learn to live with your self-awareness and own it.
I'm sure it must be exhausting trying to process your emotions all the time.
I wanna open up our relationship, while we still have it good.

Try doing more active listening in our conversation.
Why don't you wear a dress, it might feel nice. Also, feel free to go fishing this weekend. Don't worry, someone else will pick up the slack.
Who knows, maybe your parents had a positive impact in your life? Let's find out together.
What a miracle, and thank god for it! Let's give our gratitude in proper actions, and less words. Ok, in that case, let's walk on the wild side.
Let's press our foot to the accelerator, let's go 85 in a school zone!

Ahh, this is so satisfying, and we've really become a dynamic duo! Ok, stop your giggles, let's start chasing our dream and actually reaching it! We've got the doughnuts, what next? Oh right, work. Let's finish these tasks, check every item off the to-do list, then the party's starting soon. Not gonna miss it, no time to slack off! Got to keep building and moving towards that finish line! What a wild ride, did you enjoy it?
Oh shit! What did you hit! Oh, that's why we can't have nice things, just drive!

It's not as fun, but it's a ride. Ok, next. But remember, just pull over, pause the screen, and roll the fucking credits! It's time to clock out. Time to turn this bad boy off and collect our earnings. Who knew that little investment would pay off? Well, we sure did! Maybe we can buy some more guns or grenades, those things are more necessary than you think. Here, that's an island coming up, maybe we'll have a little summer villa there!
I know a guy who owns a mansion here, he'll try you nice, just don't ask questions.

Don't worry, you'll love him, trust me, he's got the time, the best cook on the beach, and he hates cats!
Ah, there's that bump, the curse of perfection. Come on, we're doing great! Don't worry, there's plenty more adventures to come. More puzzles to figure out, more stuff to kill, just a bunch of useless garbage littering the landscape of life! Ha, there's no ending, just processions and progressions!

But the journey will definitely change us, even as we move along. Can you handle this world we're living in? Will you wake up on time and greet each day with a big hearty smile? How many things can we juggle before we break? Don't hold on to that stone wall, the only way out is down.
And you say you need help, can you stop, like, being that? Thanks! There you are, my beautiful dope of a being! Let's take a minute, lean against the railing, feel the breath of wind, just...
What? That's my love language to you, my little dope, my little lovetard.

You ready for our next adventure? Well, first, can we find the next elevator? Or maybe the stairs? A tiny snack-pack pretzel awaited us at the bottom, oh well. The chase continues! There's so much adrenaline pumping through my veins, I can feel every part of me pumping as one, ready to leap over whatever wall. Let's leave behind the time of thinking about love and time, to instead embrace the now, and then beyond.
Okay, so the hallway is clear, maybe, for now, no aliens to kill, so let's go, it
, yes no aliens, no aliens, no brain melting.

Oh, the fucking smell, disgusting. You watch me at my lowest point, my self-inflicted wounds. This is what I need, what I was missing. I haven't seen a face since I started this game, and yet I know they're watching me, but more than that, feeling what I feel. Love you all. Ah, yes, thanks for the food, it's time for you to go though, you shouldn't be here.
Maybe we should be running towards instead of running away.

Let's do both.
They don't move.

They just hover in the background, like observers in a corner, waiting for you to fuck up so they can witness your suffering.
Yes, but they aren't always bad, it's just our perspective.
True.
Shake it off, it's just one little blip in a long chain of mistakes. Hey, don't frown! Tomorrow is another day.
Thanks for the memory, it's something to cling to when everything is dark. Maybe this isn't so bad, you know, maybe I'll end up finding something else, if I put my mind to it.

Boo-hoo, some stranger is robbing me of my carefully cultivated algorithms.

Be an adult and get over it.
Proctor: Perhaps this simulation has not given you the opportunity to practice healing and moving on from these sorts of things. Perhaps one of us is the problem. Ah, if you must project, you can project onto me, dear. Let me guide you to the next chapter. Don't worry, it's nothing more than an interactive to-do list for a day of fun activities! Maybe you have me to blame, maybe there are unknown variables, or maybe you are the sole cause of your actions and have no room to justify or excuse anything.

Be objective, rational, and give everyone the benefit of the doubt. Please remember that the past is your creation, not mine.
Why? Because you suck, that's why. Just like when I tell you to keep up, you slacker, you try your best, but sometimes things are too hard to do without rest. The joy in a crisis. Can you accept responsibility, or are you just going to keep on treading water? Can't you take a hint? No wonder you failed the program!

You gonna wear that?

Do you remember you lost the championship, and everyone said they would be better off without you on the team? Look at her smile, she's in charge, and you didn't even have to accept the loss. That's right, just be humble and start accepting defeat before you miss another opportunity to shine. Maybe you can build a career out of being the good loser, rather than someone who sits on their high horse and tells people what's wrong with them. You're here now, keep up!
You need some more meet on your bones, no less, way less.

Hey, good catch! Better to be helpful, intelligent, and well-prepared, rather than someone who is overwhelmed and taking up time with their mistakes. We don't have time for that. Just get it right!
As a mother, I cannot stand by and watch you neglect our child like this. Just try a little harder, you never did have any sense in this department. What else is she gonna do, ignore your calls and not answer the door? Sure, be a martyr.
I could have had an explosive acting career, but I had you.

Well, it's never too late for something to go wrong. Ah, that's the spirit! I'm rooting for you!

, we didn't! Ah, just another mistake, it's just part of the process. Really, I'm impressed with the way you're willing to take criticism and start over. Keep up the hard work!

Gosh, if you had any sense, you wouldn't spend so much time chatting.

At this rate, you might as well take a nap. Sorry, life doesn't work like that! If you keep reacting, the work will never be done.

Patient, please wait, that wasn't a condescending tone, that was frustration, maybe there's something going on internally?

who cares?

There's so much adrenaline pumping through my veins, I can feel every part of me pumping as one, ready to leap over whatever wall. Let's leave behind the time of thinking about love and time, to instead embrace the now, and then beyond.
Okay, so the hallway is clear, maybe, for now, no aliens to kill, so let's go, it
, yes no aliens, no aliens, no brain melting.

Let's do both.
They don't move.

True.
Shake it off, it's just one little blip in a long chain of mistakes. Hey, don't frown! Tomorrow is another day.

Tuning you out. They’ll wave you off, change the subject, or just plain ignore you when you want to talk about your relationship.
Actively working to turn others against you. They’ll tell co-workers, friends, and even your family that you’re unstable and prone to hysterics.
Calling you needy. When you’re really down and out and reach out for support, they’ll tell you you’re too needy or the world can’t stop turning for your little problems.
Interrupting. You’re on the phone or texting and they get in your face to let you know your attention should be on them.
Indifference. They see you hurt or crying and do nothing.
Disputing your feelings. Whatever you feel, they’ll say you’re wrong to feel that way or that’s not really what you feel at all.
--
Codependence
A codependent relationship is when everything you do is in reaction to your abuser’s behavior. And they need you just as much to boost their own self-esteem. You’ve forgotten how to be any other way. It’s a vicious circle of unhealthy behavior.

You might be codependent if you:

are unhappy in the relationship, but fear alternatives
consistently neglect your own needs for the sake of theirs
ditch friends and sideline your family to please your partner
frequently seek out your partner’s approval
critique yourself through your abuser’s eyes, ignoring your own instincts
make a lot of sacrifices to please the other person, but it’s not reciprocated
would rather live in the current state of chaos than be alone
bite your tongue and repress your feelings to keep the peace
feel responsible and take the blame for something they did
defend your abuser when others point out what’s happening
try to “rescue” them from themselves
feel guilty when you stand up for yourself
think you deserve this treatment
believe that nobody else could ever want to be with you
change your behavior in response to guilt; your abuser says, “I can’t live without you,” so you stay]
